claim: RAUC v1.15.2 system.conf 'bootloader' accepts barebox, grub, uboot, efi, custom and noop; there is no native systemd-boot backend

RAUC's efi backend supports pure EFI A/B boot: two redundant EFI partitions each holding an EFI stub kernel plus two efibootmgr boot entries pointing at the two rootfs partitions; the booted slot is found from the BootCurrent EFI variable

RAUC's custom bootloader backend is a handler that RAUC calls to get and set the primary slot and to get and set the boot state, so an integrator can drive any bootloader (e.g. systemd-boot via bootctl) without patching RAUC

RAUC 1.15.2 (released 2026-03-27) rejects 'plain'-format bundles whose payload exceeds 2 GiB, fixing CVE-2026-34155 (GHSA-6hj7-q844-m2hx): an integer overflow made the signature cover only the first few bytes of the payload
RAUC's 'bundle-formats' system.conf option is documented as 'optional, recommended' and restricts which bundle formats (e.g. plain, verity) a device accepts

Launchpad bug #2170238 (filed 2026-10-08, status New, importance Medium, linux-raspi): the Ubuntu 26.04 7.0 kernel lacks the RPi commit 'of: Improve compatibility with old Pi 5 firmware', so Pi 5 boards with a boot EEPROM older than 2025-02 stall at boot; Ubuntu 26.04 requires a 2025-02-11 or later EEPROM and some boards fail with any EEPROM from 2024-09-23 onward
TrueNAS SCALE 24.10 (24.10.0 released 2024-10-29) 'moves the applications backend from Kubernetes to Docker'; its app catalog had run on Kubernetes on single appliances before that release
Linux v6.12 verifies a module's signature with verify_pkcs7_signature(..., VERIFY_USE_SECONDARY_KEYRING, ...), i.e. against the builtin and secondary trusted keyrings only

Linux v6.12 loads the certificates in the UEFI db variable into the separate platform keyring (load_uefi.c 'Load the certs contained in the UEFI databases into the platform trusted keyring'); Kconfig describes the platform keyring as for verifying the kexec'ed kernel image and possibly the initramfs signature

Linux v6.12 Kconfig INTEGRITY_MACHINE_KEYRING: Machine Owner Keys (MOK) go to a .machine keyring that, 'unlike keys in the platform keyring', is trusted within the kernel (it depends on SECONDARY_TRUSTED_KEYRING); so a key enrolled only in UEFI db does not make modules it signed loadable, while a MOK key (enrolled via shim at the console) or a key built into the kernel does

RAUC v1.15.2 docs, 'Package-Based Distributions': 'Some non-embedded-focused distributions provide RAUC packages' (Alpine, Arch, Debian, Nix, Ubuntu); some split out a 'rauc-service' package 'as the common use of RAUC on these distributions is to create and inspect bundles, for which the D-Bus service is not required'

rauc.io home page lists 'Build System / Distro Support' (meta-rauc for Yocto/OE, Buildroot, PTXdist, Arch Linux package, 'RAUC packages available for Debian and Ubuntu', NixOS) and names no adopting product or company

[negative search result] No shipped product built on a Debian or Ubuntu root filesystem with RAUC as its A/B engine was found (three extended searches, rauc.io, RAUC docs at v1.15.2, and the existing competitor ledger, 2026-11-11). Known RAUC products are Buildroot-based (Home Assistant OS, ZimaOS) or Arch-based (SteamOS); the Debian-based constraint-matched appliance (umbrelOS) ships Rugix and earlier Mender; no shipped appliance combines Debian or Ubuntu + RAUC + k3s
